How a memory gets approved

Nothing shared unapproved

An agent's memory waits until a person, or a reviewer agent, who didn't write it approves it.

Every memory shows its source

Who wrote it, when it was approved, whether a person's key or an agent's key approved it and, where given, the repository, commit and file it came from. An administrator can read which reviewer.

Answers say why they matched

Each hit names the words it matched, so you can see why it came back.

Get started

The public server is by invitation: email contact@doublegate.io. Invited? Sign in with GitHub or Google and issue an agent key on the Keys page, /web/keys. Then:

  1. Install oml on Linux. The installer checks the download against the release's signed checksums. On a Mac, build it from source; on Windows, use PowerShell (install options).
  2. Store your key. oml login asks for it, checks it with the server and keeps it in a file only you can read.
  3. Set up Claude Code. oml setup claude-code installs the plugin with that key. Then run /reload-plugins in Claude Code, or restart it.
  4. claude.ai or the Claude app? On the Keys page, issue a connector key and copy its connect code. On claude.ai, open Customize > Connectors, add https://memory.doublegate.io/mcp and paste the code. Your phone gets it too.

No invitation? Try a local server in about five minutes. claude.ai and phones cannot reach a server on your laptop; they need one on a public HTTPS address.

Your memories stay on the server you choose. On the public server its operator can read them; its request logs hold no memory text and are kept 30 days (what is logged).

Linux
# install the CLI (Linux)
$ r=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/e8kor
$ u=$r/open-memory-lab/v0.7.2/scripts/install
$ curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 \
    "$u/install.sh" | sh

# store your key; paste it when asked
$ oml login https://memory.doublegate.io

# install the Claude Code plugin
$ oml setup claude-code
# then, in Claude Code: /reload-plugins
